Valuable Features
OpenText Functional Testing's most valuable features include expansive cross-platform and technology compatibility. Users appreciate its comprehensive support for GUI, API, mobile, web, and desktop applications. The ability to perform object identification, integrate with numerous third-party products, and utilize AI tools enhances ease of use. VBScript capability simplifies coding, while the inclusion of frameworks like BPT and LeanFT allows flexible test automation. Descriptive programming and object repository management streamline test development.
"This makes UFT the “everything and the kitchen sink” of automation tools, with an easy to learn language, a solid history, and extensive support resources."

Room for Improvement
OpenText Functional Testing could improve by offering better browser compatibility and memory optimization. Object identification is not always reliable. Users seek improvements in performance consistency, especially during long executions. Integration with modern programming languages and support for cross-browser testing are desired, as well as expanded AI functionality and lower licensing costs. Users have noted challenges with the interface and technical support response times, expressing a need for enhanced reporting features and reduced dependency on specific scripting languages.

ROI
OpenText Functional Testing is highly regarded for enhancing productivity and efficiency through automation. Companies have experienced significant returns with reduced manual labor, cutting testing times by up to 80%, and increasing testing accuracy. Users report ROI over 300% in the long term and substantial cost savings through AI capabilities. Installation on multiple machines allows users to automate traditional testing processes, achieving faster test creation and maintenance, with reduced object maintenance efforts and increased test case creation.
Pricing
Enterprise users find OpenText Functional Testing costly, with seat licenses around $10,000 and concurrent licenses approximately $17,000 including tax and maintenance. While priced higher than some alternatives, users acknowledge its comprehensive capabilities and integration with ALM/Quality Center. Many organizations opt for a mix of seat and concurrent licenses to manage costs effectively. Discounts and a variety of licensing options provide flexibility, though the model is perceived as complex and at times, confusing.

Popular Use Cases
OpenText Functional Testing is primarily used for functional testing, end-to-end testing, and UI testing. Many utilize it for automating web and desktop applications, including APIs and Oracle ERP systems. Teams employ it for regression and integration testing, leveraging its utility to automate data processing tasks and email distribution. It supports various test scenarios across cloud and on-premises environments, with ease of use enabling both technical and non-technical users to create and execute automated test scripts efficiently.
Service and Support
Many reviewers find OpenText Functional Testing's customer service knowledgeable and quick, assigning high ratings. Technical support receives mixed feedback, with some praising responsiveness and others citing slow response times and unhelpful assistance. Ratings vary, with some users finding partners more effective. Effective escalation is needed, and premium customers often receive prompt help. There are reports of complicated cases causing delays, and users desire faster solutions. The typical rating for both customer service and technical support ranges from seven to nine out of ten.
Deployment
Users found OpenText Functional Testing's initial setup mainly straightforward and easy, often aided by a wizard and installation guides. Some noted complexities, particularly involving object repositories and custom libraries. Technical familiarity eased the process for several users, while others faced challenges with licensing or add-in configurations. Deployment was manageable, typically requiring one person and taking up to a few hours, depending on technical knowledge and system specifications.
Scalability
OpenText Functional Testing is generally considered scalable, with flexibility depending on licensing and framework design. Many users scale it to meet their needs, but some encounter challenges with resource requirements and cost constraints. Expanding automation requires additional licenses, affecting costs. Users find it works well for parallel test execution, supporting large projects. It's scalable for enterprise-level use, with capabilities to integrate with various tools, adapting to different environments.
Stability
OpenText Functional Testing presents mixed stability experiences. Some users report it as highly stable, while others express crashes and inconsistency, particularly under resource constraints or certain configurations. Tools like UFT One are often noted as stable but slow. Stability sometimes depends on implementations and surrounding environments, like server capacity. Users mention that stability improves with certain setups or versions but can suffer from compatibility or resource challenges. Stability ratings vary from excellent to needing improvement.
